articles.title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle. RESULTS: A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

articles.title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To systematically review MRI-derived radiomic and artificial intelligence models predicting outcomes in men on or eligible for active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer, and whether reported endpoints permit quantitative synthesis. METHOD: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2000-September 2026). Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2, PROBAST) and methodological quality (METRICS). Three subgroups were defined: AS selection at diagnosis, baseline detection of clinically significant cancer, and progression during follow-up. Pooling was pre-specified for subgroups with at least four independent cohorts; endpoint equivalence was assessed. RESULTS: Seventeen studies across 12 unique cohorts were included. Seven publications derived from two cohorts; 12 independent cohort-level estimates (n = 2703) remained after overlap resolution. Nine publications (four independent cohorts) addressed progression (AUC 0.70 to 0.95), but progression was defined in five non-equivalent ways, from any grade-group increase to composite core-count criteria, precluding quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was high or unclear in 16 of 17 studies; the median METRICS score was 32.3 % (range 18.9-52.3 %). No study reported external validation or calibration for progression. CONCLUSIONS: Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

articles.title: Abdominal hydatid disease and its mimics: a comprehensive pictorial review of imaging clues to the differential diagnosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hydatid disease (HD), also known as echinococcosis, is a parasitic disease caused by tapeworms. HD is endemic in many parts of the world and can affect virtually any organ system. Due to the rapid growth of worldwide migration, especially in recent decades, the disease can be diagnosed anywhere, particularly among immigrants in non-endemic areas. OBJECTIVE: To illustrate the spectrum of abdominal imaging manifestations of HD and to review the principal benign and malignant abdominal cystic lesions that can mimic HD, using an organ-based approach with emphasis on imaging features that aid in differential diagnosis. FINDINGS: Radiologic imaging is crucial for diagnosing HD, assessing disease activity, progression, and complications, and detecting stage- and organ-specific features. Hydatid disease in the abdomen can mimic other abdominal diseases, depending on the organ involved. Additionally, many other abdominal lesions can mimic hydatid disease and present with similar clinical symptoms. This pictorial review demonstrates characteristic imaging findings of HD and its mimics across the different abdominal organs and spaces, highlighting specific morphological features and potential diagnostic pitfalls. This review incorporates the World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) classification to provide a standardized framework for describing the imaging appearances of cystic echinococcosis. CONCLUSION: Recognizing the characteristic imaging features of HD and its mimics is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management. A systematic approach that incorporates lesion morphology, organ involvement, disease stage, and relevant clinical and epidemiological information can improve diagnostic confidence, enable early diagnosis, and help avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention.

articles.title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Linear combination model fitting is widely used for spectral analysis in 1H-MRS but relies on basis sets with fixed spin-system parameters, implicitly neglecting the sensitivity of chemical shifts to physiological and pathological tissue microenvironments. This study systematically evaluated the impact of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis and reassessed the validity of the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) as a quality-control metric for low-concentration metabolites. METHODS: The effects of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis were investigated using simulated datasets with different baseline models and lineshapes, followed by validation in a publicly available in vivo human brain 1H-MRS dataset (n = 31). Estimated metabolite concentrations, relative concentration changes, estimation errors, and CRLB values were analyzed across all conditions. RESULTS: Frequency perturbations produced minimal quantification changes in high-concentration metabolites but substantially larger errors in several low-concentration metabolites. Across both simulations and in vivo validation, relative concentration changes generally remained below 3% for high-concentration metabolites but exceeded 10%-20% for several low-concentration metabolites, including Gln, GSH, Asp, and NAAG. Importantly, substantial estimation errors frequently occurred despite CRLB values remaining within conventionally acceptable ranges. These findings were consistently observed across different baseline models, lineshapes, and in vivo validation. CONCLUSION: Physiologically relevant frequency perturbations can introduce substantial quantification bias that is not consistently reflected by CRLB. These findings identify environmentally induced resonance-frequency variations as an underrecognized source of quantification error in current linear-combination model fitting and suggest that CRLB alone is insufficient for assessing quantification reliability, particularly under conditions associated with altered brain temperature or tissue pH.

articles.title: In Vivo Dynamic D2O-MRI for Quantifying Apparent CSF Water Renewal Across Ventricular and Extraventricular Compartments.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The choroid plexus has long been regarded as the principal source of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), yet this view remains unresolved. We developed a dynamic indirect D2O MRI approach to quantify regional apparent CSF water renewal in vivo in rats at 9.4 T. METHODS: Rats were scanned at 9.4 T using spin-echo echo-planar imaging during intravenous D2O infusion (10.69-s temporal resolution, 150 × 150 μm2 in-plane resolution). A deliberately long echo time (TE = 150 ms) was used to preferentially suppress signals from brain parenchyma, blood, and interstitial fluid, thereby enhancing sensitivity to signal changes in CSF compartments. After relaxation correction, regional apparent CSF water renewal rates were estimated using a one-compartment kinetic model. RESULTS: D2O-induced signal attenuation was regionally heterogeneous. The ambient and supracerebellar cisterns (AC + SC) exhibited the largest signal reduction, reaching 47.32% ± 15.70% of baseline, whereas the lateral ventricles (LVs) showed smaller reductions (LV1: 68.73% ± 18.72%; LV2: 72.64% ± 15.07%). The estimated apparent CSF water renewal rates were low and comparable between the bilateral ventricles (LV1: 0.20 ± 0.20 μL/min; LV2: 0.26 ± 0.21 μL/min), but markedly higher in the AC + SC region (4.38 ± 3.95 μL/min; p < 0.01 vs. LVs). The third and fourth ventricles also showed relatively small signal changes. CONCLUSION: Dynamic D2O MRI enabled noninvasive assessment of apparent CSF water renewal in vivo. The total apparent renewal rate was higher in AC + SC than in the LVs. These results suggest that extraventricular CSF compartments contribute substantially to apparent CSF water renewal.

articles.title: Depiction Fidelity and Specificity in Direct MRI of Collagen: Addressing Signal Decay at the Microsecond Timescale.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Gap-filled zero echo time (ZTE) acquisitions combined with dedicated short-T2 hardware enable direct collagen imaging on the timescale of macromolecular (MM) signals, with T2s ˜ 10 μs. However, present methods offer limited depiction fidelity, and their specificity towards MM content is poorly understood. This work presents methodology to improve depiction fidelity of MM signals and investigates how imaging parameters influence MM specificity. METHODS: 1D simulations of gap-filled ZTE sequences acquiring MM signals are used to evaluate depiction fidelity and specificity via the modulation transfer function (MTF) and point spread function (PSF). Insights are used to address signal decay at the microsecond timescale by (i) modifying the k-space sampling pattern through gap filling with MTF smoothing, (ii) selecting acquisition parameters that optimize MM specificity and (iii) designing a post-processing filter to improve resolution. The approaches are demonstrated with 3D imaging simulations and experiments. RESULTS: Gap-filled ZTE with specialized hardware targets MM signals but enters a unique imaging regime where depiction fidelity is limited: the PSF exhibits a broad main lobe from T2 blurring and far-reaching side lobes caused by a kink in the k-space sampling pattern. The latter is addressed through MTF smoothing. MM specificity is then maximized by subtracting two images acquired at different times but maintaining imaging bandwidth. Finally, post-processing filters narrow MM PSF main lobe, reducing T2 blurring and improving depiction fidelity. CONCLUSION: The investigation and developed methods improve collagen MM imaging, with potential applications for in vivo imaging or assessing materials that exhibit decay on MM timescales.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal MRI Relaxometry Phantom for T1, T2, and T1ρ Measurements.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantitative MRI (qMRI) requires quality assurance methods that reflect in vivo conditions to ensure consistent measurements with low bias and high reproducibility over time, across multiple sites, and across different MRI scanner manufacturers and models. PURPOSE: To develop a musculoskeletal (MSK) relaxometry phantom that spans the T1 and T2 (and T1ρ as an exploratory aim) ranges of articular cartilage. STUDY TYPE: Longitudinal phantom study. PHANTOM: A cylindrical phantom designed to fit within multiple knee coil configurations using dedicated support stands. The phantom contains 12 gel-filled vials spanning T1 values of 300-1200 ms, T2 values of 10-100 ms, and T1ρ values of 20-120 ms, and an MR-visible thermometer. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3T; single-echo spin-echo T2; inversion-recovery T1; spin-lock prepared T1ρ for NMR (spin-lock frequencies 300-5000 Hz) and MAPSS T1ρ for MRI (spin-lock frequency 500 Hz). ASSESSMENT: NMR and two MRI systems from different vendors were used. A prototype phantom (n = 1), production phantoms (n = 12), and matched NMR samples were evaluated. NMR data acquired at multiple temperatures served as reference and enabled temperature correction of MRI measurements. The prototype phantom was scanned longitudinally (15 measurements over 725 days) to assess stability, while production phantoms were scanned at a single timepoint to evaluate batch consistency. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Measurement variability and agreement were assessed using coefficients of variation (CVs), concordance correlation coefficients (CCCs), and Bland-Altman analysis for NMR-MRI comparison, longitudinal stability, batch consistency, and inter-vendor reproducibility. RESULTS: After temperature correction, longitudinal CVs were 1.1% (T1), 1.8% (T2), and 1.6% (T1ρ). Production phantoms showed inter-phantom CVs of 0.8% (T1), 1.2% (T2), and 0.9% (T1ρ). NMR and MRI measurements demonstrated strong agreement (CCCs > 0.99 for T1, T2, and T1ρ) with biases < 6%. Inter-vendor MRI comparisons yielded CCCs > 0.99 for T1 and T2. DATA CONCLUSION: The phantom demonstrated excellent stability and reproducibility with temperature correction, supporting its use for quality assurance in longitudinal and multisite qMRI studies. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 1. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 1.

articles.title: Sustainable iodine contrast media for a healthy future (SUSTAINED): a global survey of practice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) of the environmental impact and sustainability of iodinated contrast media (ICM). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional web-based survey was distributed to members of professional societies and advertised via social media between June and December 2024. The questionnaire covered themes including sustainability attitudes, reduction strategies, waste management, patient awareness, and institutional policies. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA). RESULTS: 231 respondents from 44 countries completed the survey, primarily diagnostic radiographers (59%) and radiologists (38%). Most respondents (60%) reported that their institutions had sustainable ICM policies, and there was a significant association between institutional size and alignment with sustainability goals    X 2  = 14.2 , p = 0.003   . Adoption of reduction strategies such as protocol optimisation, saline chasers, and multi-patient systems varied significantly across institutions    X 2  = 18.5 , p = 0.001   , with younger professionals (25-44 years) more engaged  A N O V A , F = 5.62 , p = 0.001   . Respondents reported waste management practices being inconsistently applied, with 26% of respondents reporting "never engaging"    X 2  = 19.6 , p  <  0.001   . Patient awareness was perceived as low, 47% "strongly disagreeing" that patients understood the environmental impact of ICM use    X 2  = 16.9 , p = 0.002   . Variability in KAPs across European countries was minimal    s 2  = 0.0068   . CONCLUSIONS: This survey highlights widespread professional awareness of ICM sustainability issues but reveals variability in institutional practices, limited patient awareness, and inconsistent waste management. Findings emphasise the importance of stronger institutional policies, targeted education, and international collaboration to promote sustainable ICM use. KEY POINTS: Question How do healthcare professionals perceive and implement sustainable practices in the use of iodinated contrast media (ICM) within clinical practice? Findings While many institutions endorse sustainability, notable gaps exist in waste management, patient and practitioner education, and consistency of reduction strategies. Critical relevance statement Strengthening institutional frameworks and professional and patient engagement can enhance sustainable ICM use, safeguard resources, and mitigate environmental impact.

articles.title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established. PURPOSE: To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180). CONCLUSION: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

articles.title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD). METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. RESULTS: PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set. CONCLUSION: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

articles.title: Utility of OpenEvidence and ChatGPT in Selecting Neuroimaging Based on Appropriateness Criteria.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Large Language models (LLMs) are novel tools with promising applications in imaging selection for clinical scenarios, but information is limited on the accuracy of an LLM trained on a medically specific dataset compared to a generalized dataset. In this analysis, we assessed the accuracy of the imaging recommendations by LLMs ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-5.0, and OpenEvidence for neuroradiology, using the American College of Radiology (ACR) Appropriateness Criteria as the reference standard. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prompts from the ACR Appropriateness Criteria priority clinical areas within neurology were used to build open-ended (OE) or select-all-that-apply (SATA) questions. Each question was posed three times, and the responses were scored against ACR guidelines. The performance of each LLM on OE and SATA was compared, and then was further analyzed by acuity. Mean accuracy scores were calculated by averaging performance across OE and SATA questions for each model. Analysis of variance was then conducted to assess differences in performance among the models. RESULTS: A total of 78 prompts were assessed in 11 priority clinical areas. These areas included cerebrovascular conditions, neurological pain, and spine pathologies. Amongst SATA, Open Evidence performed the best (79.5%) compared to GPT5 (71.2%) and GPT3.5 (44.4%). For the OE prompts, Open Evidence was more accurate (86.3%) than GPT3.5 (69.2%) but not GPT5 (80.6%). Amongst the models, no differences were found based on acuity. CONCLUSION: Overall, OpenEvidence performed the best for both OE and SATA prompts. ChatGPT-5 performed better than ChatGPT3.5 for SATA prompts. LLM performance was unaffected by the acuity of the case.

articles.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Uncertainty-aware auto-segmentation enables adaptive radiotherapy planning of liver metastases.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Despite remarkable auto-segmentation performance and growing clinical adoption, models frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and validate an uncertainty-aware segmentation pipeline that yields high delineation accuracy for liver cancer patients and reliably identifies safety-critical segmentation imperfections in radiotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Datasets of n = 173 patients with 224 liver metastases were divided into training (n = 100), validation (n = 33), and test (n = 40). Each case included annotated T2-weighted magnetic resonance images. An nnU-Net segmented treatment-relevant organs and provided a margin-extended hepatic mask, which served as input to a second-stage SE-ResUNet for lesion delineation. Uncertainty was approximated via checkpoint ensembling under a cyclic learning-rate schedule, yielding entropy-based uncertainty maps and case-wise uncertainty scores. These guided an adaptive post-inference analysis consisting of (i) detection of potentially missed lesions and (ii) identification of problematic contours. Performance was evaluated on 40 patients (n = 52 lesions) using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), 95%-Hausdorff-Distance (HD95), expected calibration error (ECE), uncertainty coverage, and the correlation between case-wise uncertainty scores and segmentation accuracy. RESULTS: Overall performance across treatment-relevant organs was DSC/HD95 = 0.89/4.8 mm; lesionsegmentation achieved DSC/HD95 = 0.86/4.9 mm. Uncertainty-guided post-processing, triggered in 14/40 cases, recovered 7 initially missed metastases, increasing lesion-level sensitivity from 84.6% (44/52) to 98.1% (51/52). Uncertainty estimates showed good calibration with ECE/uncertainty coverage for organs/lesion of 7.2/93.7% and 7.5/98.3%, and significant correlation between uncertainty/DSC (r = -0.802). CONCLUSION: The proposed pipeline seamlessly integrates accurate organ/lesion segmentation, interpretable uncertainty, and anatomy-guided post-processing to detect safety-critical segmentation failures and enable trustworthy AI auto-segmentation in clinical routine.

articles.title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy. METHODS AND MATERIALS: For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively. RESULTS: General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients. CONCLUSIONS: It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

articles.title: From patient-reported outcome scores to clinical meaning: defining thresholds for clinical importance for the EORTC QLQ-PR25 questionnaire for patients with prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Interpretation of patient-reported outcome scores remains challenging. Thresholds for clinical importance (TCIs) can facilitate score interpretation at the individual-patient level. We aimed to establish TCIs for the EORTC QLQ-PR25 to improve the interpretation of prostate cancer (PCa)-specific patient-reported outcomes in clinical practice and research. METHODS: In this prospective multicentre study, 261 patients with PCa from seven countries completed the EORTC QLQ-PR25 and anchor items assessing limitations in daily life, need for help/care, and worries caused by the respective symptom or problem. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were used to derive TCIs for the QLQ-PR25 scales, using a binary criterion for clinical importance based on the anchor items. Sensitivity analyses explored threshold robustness across patient subgroups. RESULTS: For five of the six QLQ-PR25 scales, ROC analyses showed acceptable to excellent discrimination, with AUC values ranging from 0.74 to 0.90. The corresponding TCIs showed sensitivity values between 0.62 and 0.88 and specificity values between 0.48 and 0.98. No meaningful threshold could be established for sexual activity (AUC = 0.48). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first TCIs for a questionnaire assessing health-related quality of life in patients with PCa. These thresholds may improve interpretation of individual patient scores, support symptom screening and clinical decision-making, and facilitate the definition of clinically meaningful outcomes in clinical research.

articles.title: Dose-effect analysis of late dental adverse effects following radiation therapy in survivors of paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcomas (HNRMS) often require radiotherapy, causing dental complications during critical development. Limited literature suggests dose-dependent risks, but clear thresholds for late dental adverse effects are lacking. This study aims to characterize dose effects on developing dentition in paediatric HNRMS patients to identify dose-response relationships informing evidence-based treatment planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Orthopantomograms from survivors of HNRMS were evaluated using the validated DENTALE scoring system. Radiation doses from brachytherapy, external beam radiation with protons and photons to deciduous teeth were retrieved from treatment plans and converted to EQD2 (α/β = 3 Gy). Dose-response relationships were modelled per tooth using binary logistic regression in Mplus (COMPLEX option for within-patient dependency; model fit assessed by ROC analysis). RESULTS: Among 34 survivors (median age at diagnosis 5.6 years), 27 (79.4 %) exhibited late dental AE. Of 919 assessable permanent teeth, 242 (26.3 %) showed abnormalities. Increasing radiation dose was consistently associated with higher AE probability. The dose corresponding to 50 % predicted probability of any dental AE was 23 Gy(EQD2). Structure-specific thresholds were higher for crowns (68 Gy) and eruption disturbances (52 Gy(EQD2)), and lower for roots (24 Gy(EQD2)) and crown-root ratio abnormalities (36 Gy(EQD2)). CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates dose-effect relationships for radiation exposure of developing dentition, with clinically relevant structure-specific thresholds. Teeth receiving no radiation still show developmental abnormalities, likely due to chemotherapy. These findings support incorporating dentition as organ at risk and dose constraints into paediatric head-and-neck radiotherapy planning to reduce dental morbidity.

articles.title: Five-Year Survival and Durable Local Control After Image-Guided Thermal Ablation for Stage IA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate five-year overall survival, cancer-specific survival, local tumor progression-free survival, local recurrence, and durable local control after repeat ablation in patients with Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer treated with image-guided thermal ablation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This HIPAA-compliant, institutional review board-approved retrospective cohort study included 85 patients with Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer treated with image-guided thermal ablation between 2011 and 2018. Patients had a single target tumor: 16 T1a, 45 T1b, and 24 T1c tumors. Outcomes included technical success, five-year overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), local tumor progression-free survival (LTPFS), local recurrence, durable local control (no further local recurrence after repeat ablation during follow-up), and adverse events. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated survival outcomes. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 55.6 months. Ablation modalities included microwave ablation in 41 patients, cryoablation in 37, and radiofrequency ablation in 7. Technical success was 100%. Grade 2 or higher adverse events within 90 days occurred in 8 patients (9.4%), all pneumothoraces requiring chest tubes. Five-year OS was 68.2%, 77.4%, and 68.2%; CSS was 100%, 87.2%, and 100%; and LTPFS was 100%, 77.8%, and 100% for T1a, T1b, and T1c tumors, respectively. Overall five-year LTPFS was 92.6%. Local recurrence occurred in 8 patients (9.4%). Six underwent repeat ablation without subsequent recurrence, yielding durable local control in 97.6%. CONCLUSION: Image-guided thermal ablation provided favorable five-year survival and high durable local control for Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer, supporting ablation as a repeatable and effective treatment option.

articles.title: Comparison of signal drop on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare signal drop percentages between in-phase and out-of-phase images on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions and evaluate their diagnostic performance in differentiating benign from malignant lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients who underwent post-contrast spine MRI with 3.0 T Dixon sequences between January 2023 and January 2024. Signal drop percentages ([in-phase - out-of-phase] / in-phase) were calculated for T2-weighted Dixon (T2 %drop) and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon images (GdT1 %drop). T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver-operating characteristic analysis with area under the curve (AUC) calculation. Optimal cutoff values were determined to achieve 100 % sensitivity for malignancy while maximizing specificity. Specificities were compared using the McNemar test. RESULTS: Among 78 patients (median age, 63.5 years [interquartile range (IQR), 54.3-70.8]; 37 men, 41 women; 41 benign, 34 malignant, and 3 indeterminate lesions), median T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were 29.2 % (IQR, 20.3-46.0) and 21.4 % (IQR, 15.4-28.6), respectively. GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop (P < 0.001). The AUC of GdT1 %drop (0.84; 95 % confidence interval [CI], 0.73-0.92) was numerically lower than that of T2 %drop (0.91; 95 % CI, 0.81-0.97), although the difference was not significant (P = 0.132). The specificity of GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than that of T2 %drop at the optimal cutoff values of 27.9 % and 29.0 %, respectively (39.0 % [95 % CI, 24.2-55.5] vs. 80.5 % [95 % CI, 65.1-91.2]; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop with substantially lower specificity, warranting cautious interpretation to avoid misclassification.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI assessment of renal Masses: Diagnostic performance of the modified clear cell likelihood score and ancillary MRI features.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and interreader agreement of the Clear Cell Likelihood Score (ccLS), the modified Clear Cell Likelihood Score (m-ccLS), and ancillary MRI features for differentiating benign from malignant renal masses and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from non-ccRCC lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 106 patients with renal masses who underwent multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) between 2018 and 2026. MRI features, including T1 signal intensity (SI) ratio, T2 SI ratio, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) ratio, and arterial-to-delayed enhancement ratio (ADER), were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis in both the overall cohort and the cT1a subgroup. Two radiologists independently assigned ccLS and m-ccLS scores and assessed the presence of a pseudocapsule for interreader agreement analysis. RESULTS: Among 106 renal masses, 73 (68.9 %) were classified as cT1a tumors. For differentiating benign from malignant renal masses, m-ccLS demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than ccLS in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.770 vs. 0.654) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.784 vs. 0.689). For differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC lesions, ccLS and m-ccLS showed comparable diagnostic performance in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.884 vs. 0.868) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.885 vs. 0.876). Among the evaluated ancillary MRI features, the T2 SI ratio was significantly associated with both benign-malignant discrimination and ccRCC identification. Interreader agreement for ccLS, m-ccLS, and pseudocapsule assessment was substantial. CONCLUSION: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

articles.title: Utility of PSA density velocity in diagnosing prostate cancer on prostate MR.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess if PSA density (PSAD) velocity is a predictor of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). METHODS: Patients undergoing prostate MR for suspected csPCa between 2017 and 2023 were included. Of these, patients who underwent two or more MR exams within 0.3 to 2 years to each other and pathological confirmation within 1 year after the last MR were identified. PI-RADS score, patient age, no-prior-PCa cohort or active surveillance (AS), PSA, PSAD, PSA-velocity and PSAD-velocity were assessed if they were predictor of csPCa. For univariate analysis, all variables were assessed using student t or chi-square tests. When variables were considered significant, variables were entered into multivariate logistic regression model. To assess whether PSAD-velocity adds diagnostic value beyond established predictors, we compared a base model (age, PI-RADS score, clinical cohort, and current PSAD) with the same model plus PSAD-velocity, using optimism-corrected AUC from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. RESULTS: 23,244 MRs were performed (17,703 for no-prior-PCa, 5,541 for AS). 1,174 patients (mean age: 65.9 years) met the inclusion criteria, and 550 (46.8%) were diagnosed with csPCa. On univariate analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (67.0 vs. 64.9 years, p<.0001), AS status (67% vs. 59%, p = .004), PSA (7.5 vs. 6.6 ng/mL, p<.001), PSAD (p<.0001), and PSAD-velocity (0.023 vs. 0.012 ng/mL/mL/year, p = .005) were associated with csPCa, but PSA-velocity (1.4 vs. 1.2 ng/mL/year, p=.38) was not. On multivariable analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (p<.0001), AS status (p = .002), PSA (p<.0001), and PSAD (p<.0001) remained significant predictors, but PSAD-velocity was not (p = .13). Adding PSAD-velocity to the base model produced no significant improvement in optimism-corrected AUC (0.7605 vs. 0.7611; ΔAUC = + 0.0006, 95% CI -0.0002 to +0.0019). CONCLUSIONS: Higher PSAD-velocity was associated with presence of csPCa on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis, and on fixed-model analysis did not meaningfully improve diagnostic discrimination beyond established predictors.

articles.title: Xenon-129 ventilation imaging in pediatric bronchiolitis obliterans patient.
Systematic review of spectral computed tomography quantitative parameters for predicting EGFR mutation status in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene mutations are important therapeutic targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Spectral computed tomography (spectral CT) has shown promise in the non-invasive prediction of EGFR status; however, the diagnostic value of these parameters remains unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the utility of key quantitative spectral CT parameters for predicting EGFR mutation status in NSCLC. METHODS: A comprehensive search of several Chinese and English databases was conducted to retrieve relevant diagnostic studies published up to October 1, 2025 that used pathology as the gold standard to assess the predictive value of spectral CT quantitative parameters for EGFR mutation detection in NSCLC. Two researchers conducted the literature screening and data extraction independently. Due to study heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. RESULTS: The quantitative parameters of spectral CT, including iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), slope of the spectral Hounsfield unit curve (λHU), and effective atomic number (Zeff), were higher in the EGFR-mutant cohort than in the wild-type cohort (P<0.05). Multi-parameter models combining quantitative parameters with clinical and imaging features showed improved diagnostic performance. The results were unaffected by the various brands of CT scanners and their scanning parameters. CONCLUSIONS: Several quantitative parameters derived from spectral CT are associated with EGFR mutations in NSCLC. Predictive models integrating these quantitative parameters with imaging features and clinical variables may further improve diagnostic efficacy. This may inform epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) planing. Large-scale prospective studies are needed to validate these models.

articles.title: Deep learning-based segmentation, grading and genotype classification of glioma: a literature analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Glioma represents the most prevalent and lethal primary brain tumor in adults, and its high mortality poses a significant challenge to clinical decision-making. While the conventional gold standard for diagnosis relies on the examination of surgically resected tumor tissue, recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have demonstrated compelling performance in medical image analysis, offering the potential for non-invasive prediction of the genetic and histological features of glioma as well as automatic tumor segmentation. This review aims to comprehensively summarize deep learning-based techniques for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Xplore, and Scopus for articles published in English between January 2014 and December 2025, using combinations of the terms "glioma", "brain tumor", "deep learning", "convolutional neural network", "segmentation", "classification", "grading", "genotype", "isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)", "1p/19q", and "O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT)". Peer-reviewed studies that applied deep learning methods to glioma analysis using medical imaging data and reported quantitative performance results were included, whereas review articles without original results, studies using exclusively non-deep-learning methods, and studies focused solely on non-glioma brain tumors were excluded. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: This review first summarizes the commonly used public datasets [Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS), The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), synthetic, and private cohorts] and performance metrics, and then surveys deep learning-based approaches for glioma segmentation, grading, and genotype classification according to task. Recent methodological advances, including Vision Transformers, foundation models such as the segment anything model (SAM) and MedSAM, diffusion models, and self-supervised learning, are also discussed. Reported performance varies considerably across datasets and evaluation protocols, and risks of bias, including slice-level data leakage, patient overlap across public repositories, and single-center confounding, remain prevalent in the genotype prediction literature. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning has become a transformative tool for non-invasive glioma characterization. Future research should prioritize prospective multi-center validation, standardized evaluation protocols, calibrated uncertainty estimation, and clinically deployable frameworks, thereby facilitating the translation of these techniques into routine diagnostic workflows and ultimately improving outcomes for patients with glioma.

articles.title: Evaluation of the brachial plexus and spinal cord with diffusion tensor imaging and synthetic MRI in obstetric brachial plexus palsy: DTI of brachial plexus and spinal cord in OBPP.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Obstetric brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) is conventionally staged as a peripheral nerve injury, yet conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) poorly reflects microstructural neural and spinal cord changes. We evaluate whether magnetic resonance image compilation (MAGIC), a form of synthetic MRI, shows strong agreement with conventional T2-weighted short-tau inversion recovery (T2-STIR) for postganglionic injury detection, compare diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics between injured and adjacent intact segments of the brachial plexus and spinal cord, and explore whether these metrics predict recovery at 2-year follow-up in infants with OBPP. METHODS: In this single-center cohort with prospective enrollment and ambispective outcome assessment, 40 infants (aged 3-30 weeks) with unilateral OBPP underwent 3-T MRI during physiological sleep, comprising conventional T2-STIR, synthetic MRI (MAGIC T2-STIR), and DTI. Two blinded neuroradiologists compared synthetic and conventional sequences for postganglionic lesion detection (weighted κ). The DTI-derived fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) were measured at the neural foramen (dorsal root ganglion level) and spinal cord at every injured segment and at the nearest intact segments above and below; per infant, the minimum injured value and the mean intact value were compared and related to Narakas type and 2-year recovery. RESULTS: Synthetic MRI showed strong agreement with conventional T2-STIR (κ = 0.84-1.00); the intraobserver repeatability of DTI measurements was good to excellent [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) = 0.842-0.999), except for intact spinal cord ADC (ICC = 0.662). Compared with intact reference segments, injured segments showed lower FA and higher ADC at both the neural foramen (FA = 0.236 ± 0.092 vs. 0.433 ± 0.130; ADC = 2,116 ×10-6 vs. 1,191.25 ×10-6 mm2/s) and the spinal cord (FA = 0.321 ± 0.107 vs. 0.448 ± 0.143; ADC = 2,253.5 ×10-6 vs. 1,191 ×10-6 mm2/s) (all P < 0.001). Neither FA nor ADC differed by Narakas type or predicted 2-year recovery. CONCLUSION: Synthetic MRI showed strong agreement with conventional T2-STIR for the detection of postganglionic OBPP and provided six contrasts from a single acquisition of similar duration; DTI abnormalities at injured segments extended to the spinal cord, suggesting that microstructural change in OBPP may not be confined to the peripheral nerve. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Segmental DTI abnormality within the spinal cord raises the possibility that OBPP injury extends centrally; confirmation would require higher-resolution acquisition, technical validation against partial-volume and cerebrospinal fluid effects, and larger longitudinal cohorts before any implication for injury classification.

articles.title: Nomogram models integrating multiregion radiomics, quantitative computed tomography, and clinical indicators for distinguishing connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and improving the prediction of gender-age-physiology stage.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), along with assessment of the interstitial lung disease gender-age-physiology (ILD-GAP) index, is crucial for formulating effective therapeutic interventions. The aim of this study was to examine whether multiregion radiomics combined with clinical indicators and quantitative computed tomography (QCT) can enhance the diagnostic accuracy for IPF and CTD-ILD. We also assessed the potential of radiomics as a noninvasive alternative to pulmonary function testing (PFT) for evaluating ILD-GAP staging, a prognostic marker. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with IPF and CTD-ILD at two centers. Honeycombing (H), reticulation (R), and ground-glass opacity (GGO) were outlined in representative regions, and radiomics features were then extracted. Multidimensional data included multiregional radiomics, QCT (lesion volume), and clinical indicators. The most appropriate machine learning algorithms were selected to develop models. Ultimately, the logistic regression algorithm was employed to establish a nomogram model for distinguishing IPF from CTD-ILD and a nomogram gender-age-physiology (nomogram-GAP) model for predicting ILD-GAP staging. Model performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: To differentiate IPF from CTD-ILD, we enrolled patients from Center A into training (n=153), test (n=64), and internal validation (n=42) sets, as well as 40 patients from Center B into an external validation set. The nomogram model yielded an AUC of 0.854 in the internal validation set and 0.823 in the external validation set. For ILD-GAP staging prediction, Center A patients were split into training (n=155) and internal validation sets (n=31). The nomogram-GAP model had an AUC of 0.881 in the internal validation set. Calibration and DCA demonstrated that the nomogram model and nomogram-GAP model exhibit strong consistency and clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: Two types of nomograms integrating multiregion radiomics, QCT, and clinical indicators demonstrated promising performance in distinguishing IPF from CTD-ILD and predicting ILD-GAP staging. When PFTs are unreliable or impracticable, the nomogram-GAP model may serve as a reliable marker for assessing ILD-GAP staging.

articles.title: Prediction of patient-specific quality assurance for volumetric modulated arc therapy using machine log files.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep learning (DL) models have been used for predicting gamma passing rates (GPRs) of patient specific quality assurance (PSQA) in volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). As the model input mostly from planning parameters and dose distribution, the effect of motion precision of the treatment machine has frequently been ignored. In this study,the most recent motion precision of multi-leaf collimator (MLC) leaves was estimated by their records in machine log file and used jointly with the beam intensity map to predict GPRs of VMAT PSQA. METHODS: The input of the DL model consists of two parts: the MLC positional error map which was estimated from machine log file and the beam intensity map which was obtained from the treatment plan. A UNet++ model was trained to predict the GPR of VMAT PSQA. The effect of feature maps and time intervals in estimating MLC leaf positional error maps on the prediction accuracy was evaluated. In addition, the proposed model was compared with two competing DL models (ResNet and SE-Net) and a classic regression model. The prediction error was quantified by mean absolute errors (MAEs) under two clinical accepted criteria (3%-3 mm and 3%-2 mm). Pearson's correlation coefficient (r) between measured and predicted GPR was also assessed. RESULTS: The model with the inputs of beam intensity and MLC leaf positional error maps achieved the best performance among all combinations with various input feature maps. The MAEs predicted by the proposed model with MLC leaf positional error map obtained from 5 days' records were 0.90 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.74 for 3%-2 mm criterion, whereas those predicted by the proposed model with MLC leaf positional error map obtained from 1 day's record were 1.01 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.85 for 3%-2 mm criterion. The proposed model achieved the smaller MAEs (1.01 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 1.85 for 3%-2 mm criterion) than the other two competing models: ResNet (2.85 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 2.83 for 3%-2 mm criterion) and SE-Net (3.53 for 3%-3 mm criterion and 4.55 for 3%-2 mm criterion). CONCLUSIONS: The proposed model that combines beam intensity map and MLC leaf positional error map exhibited a better prediction performance for GPRs of VMAT PSQA. It would be advantageous to include more motion precision information of treatment machine into DL models for high-performance prediction of VMAT PSQA.

articles.title: Nodule subtype dependency of CT-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of spread through air spaces in stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a multi-centre study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spread through air spaces (STAS) is an important invasive pattern associated with aggressive behaviour and prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma. However, whether nodule subtype influences the performance of computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics for preoperative STAS prediction remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of nodule subtype on CT-based radiomics performance for STAS prediction in stage I lung adenocarcinoma. METHODS: This was a multi-centre retrospective study, with 1,377 patients in the internal cohort and 436 in the external validation cohorts. Two radiomics models were developed: an all-subtype model (M1) and a pure-solid-specific model (M2). Radiomic features were obtained from preoperative CT images, and model development was performed using Extreme Gradient Boosting. Predictive performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and decision-curve analysis. In the external pure-solid cohort, the two models were directly compared using the DeLong test, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: M1 yielded an AUC of 0.839 in the internal cohort and 0.865 in the overall external cohort. After external stratification by nodule subtype, the AUCs for non-solid and pure-solid nodules were 0.797 and 0.788, respectively. M2 yielded an AUC of 0.773 in the internal cohort and 0.768 in the external cohort. In the external pure-solid cohort, M1 exhibited superior discrimination (P=0.0018), while M2 yielded more favourable reclassification performance (NRI =0.643; IDI =0.184). CONCLUSIONS: CT-based radiomics may have value for preoperative STAS prediction; however, its predictive performance likely depends on nodule subtype, with pure-solid nodules representing the primary diagnostic challenge.

articles.title: The utility of patient symptom questionnaires in CT of the lumbosacral spine.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower back pain and radiculopathy impose significant burdens on healthcare systems. Computed tomography (CT) scans are often used as an imaging modality for lower back symptomatology in the community. Accurately identifying relevant symptom sources using CT scans is often challenging due to the high incidence of incidental structural abnormalities. We examine the effectiveness of patient questionnaires in assisting reporting of CT scans of the lumbosacral spine. METHODS: In this retrospective audit, a questionnaire was provided to 250 consecutive patients undergoing lumbar spine CT prior to their scan being reported. Questions addressed the type of symptoms, such as pain and/or altered sensation, the location of these, and previous investigations. These questionnaires were provided with the lumbar spine CT scans, which were then reported by a pool of 30 radiologists. RESULTS: Of the 250 questionnaires administered, one was excluded from analysis as peer-review feedback identified inconsistency with the inclusion criteria. Of the 249, 214 questionnaires were completed and included for further analysis. Of the 214 patients who completed the questionnaire, 211 of them had back pain (98.6%) whilst 3 (1.4%) did not. One hundred sixty-four (76.6%) patients had lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms (altered sensation or limb pain) whilst 50 (23.4%) did not. Of the 214 patients with completed questionnaires, 184 radiological reports referenced the questionnaires (86%), whereas 30 (14%) did not. Of the 214 patients, 33 (15.4%) had clinical request information that suggested alternate pathology to what was indicated on the questionnaire. In these 33 cases, 28 (84.8%) radiological reports made direct reference to the patient questionnaire. For the 164 patients with lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms, 24 (14.6%) had incongruent clinical request information with questionnaires. In these 24 cases, 19 (79.2%) had radiological reports which made reference to the questionnaire. For the 50 patients with lower back pain as their sole symptom, 9 (18%) had incongruent clinical request information with questionnaires. In all 9 (100%) of these cases, radiological reports referenced the questionnaires. The questionnaire identified that 199 out of 214 patients (93%) had external lower back imaging available. CONCLUSIONS: Inclusion of a symptom questionnaire has benefit to the reporting radiologist. We observed a high completion and usage rate of the questionnaire, which may indicate feasible use in regular workflows. Importantly, we noted that patient questionnaires help with providing accurate clinical information and are especially important for cases in which there are differing accounts of patient symptomatology, both for patients with lumbar spine-related sensory symptoms and for those with lower back pain as a sole symptom. Furthermore, they can inform radiologists when external lower back imaging is available. These factors can assist the radiologist in providing higher quality reports, ideally resulting in better patient outcomes.

articles.title: Possible hemodynamic mechanisms in the size change of cerebral aneurysms: an exploratory study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In asymptomatic small unruptured intracranial aneurysms (IAs), growth is one of the important factors determining treatment to prevent rupture and hemorrhage. Hemodynamic factors play a crucial role in the growth and regression of aneurysms, although the mechanisms involved are not yet clear. The aim of this study was to investigate the hemodynamic mechanisms underlying size changes in small unruptured IAs (<7 mm) during follow-up. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 63 patients with unruptured IAs (<7 mm) who underwent computed tomography angiography (CTA) imaging follow-up for more than 6 months. Aneurysm hemodynamic and morphological parameters were measured by software AneuFlow. Statistical comparisons were performed between enlarging aneurysms and stable aneurysms. RESULTS: Enlarging aneurysms (43/63, 68%) exhibited a significantly higher baseline wall shear stress (WSS) (7.98 vs. 5.76 Pa, P=0.04) and a borderline higher WSS gradient (WSSG) (9.83 vs. 5.62 Pa/mm, P=0.05) compared to stable aneurysms. During enlargement, WSSG decreased (P=0.04), while parent vessel diameter increased (P<0.01), accompanied by reduced parent vessel WSS (P<0.01). In 30% of growing cases, parent vessel expansion was correlated with marked WSS and WSSG reduction in the aneurysm, suggesting adaptive remodeling. Low normalized WSS (NWSS) was correlated with decrease in diameter of the parent vessel (Dvessel) (r=0.30, P=0.02) and aneurysm surface area (r=0.36, P<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: This study analyzed the effect of hemodynamics on the size change of aneurysms. High WSS and high WSSG may be inducing factors for aneurysm enlargement, while high WSS may lead to expansion of the parent vessel. In the early stages of aneurysm development, low WSS may contribute to size reduction.

articles.title: Predictive models for trans-stenotic pressure gradient in the transverse sinus based on multimodal correlates.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The invasive nature of the methods currently available for screening based on the trans-stenotic pressure gradient (TPG) limits their widespread application. We aimed to develop machine learning models for predicting TPG in the transverse sinus. METHODS: The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Beijing Friendship Hospital Affiliated to Capital Medical University. We retrospectively analyzed the data of 83 patients confirmed to have pressure-measured transverse sinus stenosis from January 2017 to June 2022 at Beijing Friendship Hospital. The dataset included clinical, laboratory, computed tomography angiography, and four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance data with 29 feature indicators. Six machine learning methods-support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, decision tree, random forest (RF), gradient boosting decision tree, and extreme gradient boosting-were employed to construct classification models for 4- and 8-mmHg TPG thresholds via fivefold cross-validation. Models were evaluated according to accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: For the 4-mmHg threshold, RF showed the highest performance, with an accuracy of 0.83, a specificity of 0.62, a sensitivity of 0.95, an F1 score of 0.92, an MCC of 0.60, and an AUC of 0.92. RF also excelled for the 8-mmHg threshold, with accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, F1 score, MCC, and AUC values of 0.84, 0.86, 0.81, 0.78, 0.70, and 0.91, respectively. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis indicated that peak velocity and average velocity differences positively correlated with TPG, whereas the residual area ratio was negatively correlated. CONCLUSIONS: The models demonstrated strong discriminative ability and are useful for noninvasive TPG prediction.

articles.title: Quantitative dual-energy computed tomography parameters as imaging biomarkers for assessing the histopathologic grade of colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global healthcare burden. Tumor differentiation grade is a critical prognostic factor for evaluating patients with CRC. The objective of this study was to examine the value of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) quantitative parameters as imaging biomarkers for the preoperative prediction of histopathologic CRC grade. METHODS: A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced DECT were enrolled and divided into low-grade (n=74) and high-grade (n=43) groups. Monoenergetic 74-keV images from the arterial phase (AP), venous phase (VP), and delayed phase (DP) were reconstructed as conventional 120 kVp-like computed tomography (CT) images. Lesion CT attenuation values, iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and extracellular volume (ECV) were measured in three phases by two radiologists, and clinical data were collected. Intergroup comparisons and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted to determine the associations between spectral parameters and the histopathologic grade of CRC, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were applied to identify independent correlates. Three types of predictive models were established: a baseline model incorporating clinical variables and CT attenuation values, a single spectral parameter model, and combined models integrating clinical features with different spectral parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and the DeLong test were used to compare the area under the curve (AUC) between the models. Bootstrap internal validation with 1,000 resamples was performed on the optimal model. RESULTS: Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration showed significant differences between the low-grade group and high-grade group (P=0.009), whereas triphasic 120 kVp-like CT attenuation values showed no statistical differences (P>0.05). For the AP, only IC differed significantly (P=0.011); for the VP and DP, IC, NIC, Zeff, and ECV differed significantly (P<0.05), with ECV showing the strongest correlation with histopathologic grade in CRC (r=0.650: P<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified VP IC [odds ratio (OR) =4.601; P=0.046] and ECV (OR =1.492; P<0.001) as independent correlates of high histopathologic grade in CRC, with AUCs of 0.749 and 0.889, respectively. The integrated model combining clinical indicators with VP and DP spectral parameters achieved the best performance for predicting high histopathologic grade in CRC [AUC =0.904, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.845-0.962; bias‑corrected AUC =0.904, 95% CI: 0.837-0.954], with an accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of 85.5%, 88.4%, and 83.8%, respectively. The DeLong test revealed that this integrated model had significantly better diagnostic performance than did the baseline model (AUC =0.538; P<0.001), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed between the integrated model and the VP + DP dual-phase model (P=0.504). CONCLUSIONS: DECT quantitative parameters have potential clinical value for predicting the histopathologic grade of patients with CRC. They may serve as imaging biomarkers and provide valuable information for understanding tumor biological behavior.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of a multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging-based nomogram incorporating apparent diffusion coefficient in preoperative differentiation of phyllodes tumors from breast cancer: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative differentiation between phyllodes tumors (PTs) and breast cancers (BCs) remains a clinical challenge due to their overlapping imaging characteristics. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), incorporating morphological, hemodynamic, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) parameters, to develop a nomogram model for differentiating PTs from BCs, and to preliminarily explore the association between ADC parameters and the histologic grade of PTs. METHODS: A total of 92 patients (mean age, 46.04 years) with pathologically confirmed PTs (n=31) or BCs (n=61) who underwent 3.0 Tesla (T) breast MRI at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between June 2018 and June 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Multiparametric MRI features, including morphological characteristics, hemodynamic parameters, and quantitative diffusion metrics [mean ADC (ADCmean) and relative ADC (rADC)], were assessed for all lesions. Intergroup differences were compared using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Mann-Whitney U test or Kruskal-Wallis H test, Chi-squared test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors and construct a diagnostic nomogram. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curve analysis. Finally, 5-fold internal cross-validation was used to assess the model's stability. RESULTS: PTs were characterized predominantly by a lobulated morphology, hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and T2 hypointense septations, whereas BCs typically presented as irregular masses with spiculated margins and peritumoral edema. Regarding dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) features, PTs predominantly demonstrated rapid initial enhancement with heterogeneous or dark internal septations, and time-intensity curves (TICs) mainly exhibited Type I/II patterns. PTs demonstrated significantly higher ADCmean, rADC1 (lesion-to-pectoralis muscle ratio), and rADC2 (lesion-to-contralateral gland ratio) values compared with the BCs (all P<0.001). Subgroup analysis revealed a stepwise decrease in ADCmean from benign PTs to borderline/malignant PTs and BCs. The diagnostic nomogram integrating T2WI signal intensity, T2 hypointense septations, TIC pattern, and ADCmean achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.997. Following rigorous internal 5-fold cross-validation with Firth's penalty to mitigate potential overfitting, the model maintained a robust average AUC of 0.978 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.951-1.000]. DCA demonstrated the net clinical benefit of the combined model. CONCLUSIONS: Multiparametric MRI provides significant diagnostic value in preoperatively differentiating PTs from BCs. Although the subgroup analysis regarding PT histological grading remains preliminary due to limited sample sizes, both ADCmean and rADC offer valuable quantitative insights, with rADC serving as a complementary metric. Crucially, the combined diagnostic nomogram demonstrated robust diagnostic performance despite internal penalization. Pending prospective external validation, this tool may inform individualized diagnosis and optimize surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Single-view echocardiography-based deep learning for pulmonary hypertension detection: a multi-level supervised and explainable approach.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early identification of pulmonary hypertension (PH), particularly mild disease, remains challenging. We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model for noninvasive PH screening using single-view transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), without reliance on Doppler measurements. METHODS: In this retrospective study, apical four-chamber (A4C) TTE cine loops were collected between January 2023 and June 2025. A total of 144 patients with PH confirmed by right heart catheterization (RHC), 17 RHC-confirmed non-PH patients, and 95 non-PH controls defined by TTE under strict inclusion criteria were included. An additional temporally independent validation cohort of 40 RHC-confirmed subjects was enrolled between December 2025 and May 2026. Multiple DL architectures were evaluated for detecting PH. Model performance was assessed at both sample and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: A total of 256 patients with 318 TTE examinations were included for model development and independent validation, and an additional 40 RHC-confirmed subjects with 40 TTE examinations were included for temporal validation. The multi-level supervised model achieved the best performance among the evaluated architectures, with a patient-level AUROC of 1.000 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.998-1.000], sensitivity of 0.954, and specificity of 1.000 in the independent validation cohort. In the temporal validation cohort, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.843-0.992), with sensitivity of 0.875, specificity of 0.813, and accuracy of 0.850. In an analysis of 50 RHC-confirmed subjects, the DL model achieved an AUROC of 0.937 (95% CI: 0.865-0.987) for distinguishing mild PH from non-PH, with sensitivity of 0.857 and specificity of 0.864, compared with AUROCs of 0.607-0.825 for conventional echocardiographic parameters. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable DL framework based on single-view A4C echocardiography for noninvasive PH assessment. The model showed promising performance, including preserved sensitivity for mild PH. Further multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Impact of hypertriglyceridemia on right ventricular deformation in patients with left ventricular myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a significant risk factor for myocardial infarction (MI), adversely affecting left ventricular (LV) structure and function and worsening clinical outcomes. Given the interaction between ventricles, the right heart may also be affected by MI. This study investigated the additional effects of HTG on right ventricular (RV) deformation in patients with acute MI. METHODS: The study included 101 patients with MI [58 without HTG (HTG-) and 43 with HTG (HTG+)] and 83 control participants, all of whom underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The patients with MI were categorized into HTG+ and HTG- subgroups. RV and LV function and strain were assessed, and multivariate linear regression was performed to identify determinants of RV peak strain (PS). RESULTS: Compared with the HTG- group, the HTG+ group exhibited higher total cholesterol and troponin levels (P=0.002 and P=0.043, respectively), as well as significantly lower RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05 after Bonferroni correction). RV radial PS was inversely correlated with LV mass (r=-0.349, P=0.021), total cholesterol (r=-0.402, P=0.007), troponin (r=-0.584, P<0.001), and infarct size (r=-0.410, P=0.006). RV circumferential PS was correlated with multiple LV parameters, lipids, and infarct extent (r=0.323 to 0.574; all P<0.05). After adjusting for age, sex, and blood pressure, HTG remained independently associated with impaired RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: HTG is associated with greater RV strain impairment in patients with MI. Our findings suggest that triglyceride levels and LV infarct extent may be associated with RV strain impairment, warranting further investigation in prospective studies.

articles.title: The added value of contrast-enhanced ultrasonography to BI-RADS in the evaluation of breast lesions presenting with pathological nipple discharge.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological nipple discharge (PND) is a frequent presentation in breast clinics, yet its accurate differentiation between benign and malignant lesions remains difficult due to the inherent limitations of current imaging tools. There is still a lack of a practical, non‑invasive approach that incorporates contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features with the conventional Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) to improve the diagnostic yield. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and diagnostic performance of a rerated BI-RADS system combining ultrasound (US) and CEUS versus US BI-RADS alone for breast lesions causing PND. METHODS: A total of 217 consecutive patients with PND underwent conventional US and CEUS between January 2009 and August 2025. Each lesion was evaluated with US BI-RADS categories, then CEUS BI-RADS categories were re-rated based on US BI-RADS categories and CEUS scores. All responsible lesions were confirmed by pathological results through surgery or biopsy. To account for the potential correlation among multiple lesions from the same patient, we used generalized estimating equations with an exchangeable correlation structure for multivariate analysis to identify independent risk factors. The diagnostic performance of US BI-RADS and CEUS BI-RADS was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. RESULTS: There were 258 breast lesions from 217 patients consecutively evaluated in this retrospective study. A total of 57 lesions were pathologically confirmed to be malignant, and 201 were confirmed to be benign. There was a statistically significant difference in multiple clinical and ultrasonic features between malignant and benign lesions (P<0.05). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis based on generalized estimating equations identified age, size, enhancement range, enhancement order and spiculate sign as independent predictors of malignant breast lesions with discharge (all P<0.02). The BI-RADS categories based on CEUS showed higher sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) compared to US BI-RADS, which were 0.930 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.822-0.977], 0.945 (95% CI: 0.858-0.982) and 0.637 (95% CI: 0.575-0.695), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, CEUS BI-RADS demonstrates high sensitivity and NPV in evaluating breast lesions associated with PND. Although its overall discriminatory ability, as measured by AUROC, was not significantly different from that of conventional US BI-RADS when BI-RADS 4a lesions were considered test-positive, CEUS provides complementary functional information that aids in risk stratification. These findings position CEUS as a valuable adjunct to conventional US, particularly in refining the assessment of low-suspicion lesions and guiding biopsy decisions in patients with PND.
